raw_response:
I've been farming these 7 mu for 30 years now. I'm 51, and honestly the work gets harder every year, especially my knees after all that bending in the cotton fields. My husband works construction in Handan and sends money home when he can, and my son got a job in Shijiazhuang last year, so it's mostly me and my mother-in-law handling the day-to-day. We have 5 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 2 mu in cotton. Money is always tight on a farm this small — I can't just buy whatever the extension office recommends. I buy fertilizer in small bags as I need it, and I watch every yuan.

For the wheat that's already in the ground: I planted it last October around the 10th with a variety I've used for years — it's not the newest thing but I know how it behaves here. I already put down base fertilizer in the fall. Now in spring, I topdress about 10 kg of urea per mu when the wheat greens up, around early April. The extension guy said I could go up to 15 kg, but urea got more expensive this year and my wheat looks decent, so I'll stick with what I know. I irrigate three times — green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Each time costs me about 12 yuan per mu for electricity to pump, so that's 180 yuan just for wheat water. I sprayed herbicide once already, and I'll watch for aphids but I won't spray unless I see them.

For cotton on my 2 mu: I'll plant around April 20th once the soil warms up. I use a local cotton seed, not those expensive hybrids. I put about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting, and if the plants look weak at flowering I'll topdress with another 6 kg of urea. Cotton needs water at planting and during flowering — two irrigations. But the real cost is insecticides. Bollworm always comes, and aphids too. I spray four times through the season, buying generic products from the village store. It runs about 70 yuan per mu for chemicals.

For summer maize: This is always the most stressful part. I harvest wheat around June 8th, and I have maybe 4 days to get maize in the ground or I lose growing season. I hire a tractor with a planter to clear the wheat stubble and plant — costs 40 yuan per mu. I buy hybrid maize seed, about 50 yuan per mu. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu all at planting — I don't have time for split applications in this double-crop system. If the summer rains are good, maize doesn't need much extra water. I'll irrigate once at the V6 stage if it's dry, and maybe once at tasseling if there's no rain. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once.

Labor is my biggest problem. I do almost everything myself. For wheat harvest I hire two people for two days because I can't cut and thresh fast enough alone. For maize harvest in September I hire three people for two days — the window is tight and cotton is also needing attention then. Cotton picking is the worst — it's all hand work and takes five or six passes through the field from September to October. I pick it myself over several weeks, doing a little each day between other chores. I can't afford to hire pickers at 80 yuan per day.

My total input budget this year is about 2,800 yuan. That's a stretch — I have to buy things bit by bit. I expect about 380 kg per mu from wheat, 450 kg per mu from maize, and about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton. If prices hold and we don't get a drought, that should cover my costs and leave a little for household expenses.
